status: proposal only; no archive removed and no cache artifact migrated
leave_untouched: all checked proof source and native-checker source/configuration
runtime_evidence: ldd of checklemma, lean and lake contains no .a dependencies; checklemma.trace depends on source object/link arguments/toolchain identity but no archive file hashes
steps: Root reviews and pushes current checker-setup archive before mutations.
Delete only explicit .a files from verified inventory; these are reproduced by the official pinned Lean toolchain release, and no new native link is planned.

Copy selected newly fetched memory cache artifacts to ordinary files beside their current symlinks; verify original manifest SHA256 and byte count, preserve mode/timestamps, then atomically replace symlink with regular file.

For every remaining new artifact, a new holder opens the existing sealed memfd through /proc/old-pid/fd/old-fd read-only, verifies manifest SHA256, and atomically replaces symlink with its new holder path. This retains the same sealed inode without duplicating artifact bytes.

Keep every old holder alive until every original artifact is either a verified regular disk file or held by a verified new holder. Preserve all artifact types; no editor/generated-source metadata is dropped.

Only after complete manifest reconciliation, request normal old-loader STOP. Its cleanup deletes only unchanged old symlinks, so already transferred paths survive. Closing old FDs releases the migrated memory-backed bytes.

Run a short genuine Lean/build preflight, then unchanged official checker under the same external memory guard if parent renews lease. Preserve full logs and do not infer acceptance from import/build alone.
limits: May still be insufficient for the full checker.
Static archives would need official restoration if a future native relink is necessary.
No Mathlib source build, checker configuration edits, fake artifacts, preload shims, or unapproved host access.
Any transfer failure before old-loader STOP retains all original source bytes.
